title: ARD section 9 - Special action animations

container.notes: ARD section 9 (special action animations; NOT st2e: u32 count, 12 unread bytes, rows of 16 bytes from 0x10; empty = 32 zero bytes). ARD = standalone *.ard or section 19 of an .ebp: 8-byte magic FF12AR03, ten u32 section offsets at 0x08 relative to the ARD start (0 = absent; this section = u32 at ARD+0x2C); sections 0,2..9 written in index order on 16-byte boundaries with zero fill, section 1 written last with nothing after it. A section spans to the next larger non-zero offset (the highest to the end of the ARD).

records.name: header
records.where: Offset 0 of ARD section 9 (ARD start + u32 at ARD+0x2C).

fields.name: entryCount
fields.notes: Number of 16-byte rows that start at section offset 0x10.

fields.name: unknown04
fields.notes: Not read; zero in Workshop output.

fields.name: weaponStance
fields.notes: Weapon stance the entry applies to (stance id; compare BpWeaponStanceList - list assignment not confirmed).

fields.name: actionCharacterAnimationLink
fields.notes: Character-animation id used by actions (links an action's character animation to this entry).

fields.name: animationFileLink
fields.notes: Which animation file to use (the Toolkit's file viewer has a "Foe Special Action Animation" file type, TK L1411).

fields.name: unknown0A
fields.notes: Not read; the Workshop writes six zero bytes.

roundTrip: Edit fields in place; nothing inside the section points anywhere.
Keep the 12 bytes at 0x04-0x0F and the six trailing bytes of each row as read.
An empty section stays 32 zero bytes (do not shrink it to 16 or drop it).
Adding or removing rows: update entryCount; the section grows/shrinks by 16 per row.

If this section changes length, rebuild the ARD offset table: every section stored after it moves (recompute their u32 slots, keep 16-byte starts with zero fill, keep section 1 last with nothing after it); if the ARD sits in EBP section 19, the EBP offsets after section 19 move as well.
gaps: Meaning of the 12 bytes after entryCount and of the six bytes at 0x0A-0x0F of each row.
Which list weaponStance uses (battlepack weapon stance rows or the stance animation list).
Id space of actionCharacterAnimationLink and animationFileLink (likely the battlepack action character-animation ids and the foe special action animation files).
Why an empty table is 32 bytes long.
